problem_statement: The paper frames the problem as US banks needing to prevent increasingly sophisticated financial crime and fraud in a digital, real-time banking environment. It also treats financial security as a broader challenge that includes fraud detection, cyber threats, encryption protection, and risk management.
problem_statement_quotes: Criminals have traditionally been able to exploit vulnerabilities on the part of the financial sector and banks.
In the United States, banks handle billions of transactions daily, making them attractive to fraudsters, cybercriminals, and money launderers.
The problem facing US banks is at a crucial moment of financial security.
classical_baseline: The paper says banks currently rely on conventional computing, rule-based systems, machine learning models, and traditional encryption such as RSA and ECC to detect fraud and protect data. It also mentions existing security frameworks and traditional risk models as the current baseline.
classical_baseline_quotes: banks have sunk money into fraud detection systems, artificial intelligence (AI) and block chain technology to beef up defenses against such attacks.
But, conventional computing has limitations, especially when it comes to interactively querying and processing massive data at high-speed [2].
Generally, most banks use rule based systems and machine learning algorithms to catch the fraud by flagging the suspicious transactions on the basis of patterns that are pre-defined.
They also rely on traditional security infrastructures through RSA and ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography)
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical approaches struggle with massive transaction volumes, high-speed processing, evolving fraud tactics, false positives and false negatives, limited response time, and the inability to keep up with real-time payments. It also says current encryption will become vulnerable to quantum attacks.
classical_difficulty_quotes: But, conventional computing has limitations, especially when it comes to interactively querying and processing massive data at high-speed [2].
The challenges faced by the US banking in the area of financial crime are developing constantly and fraudsters do not stop inventing new and more sophisticated techniques to bend the banking systems.
Many legitimate transactions become marked as fraudulent, which results in customer discontent and operational inefficiencies [17].

business_stakes: The paper says the stakes include protecting sensitive customer data, maintaining financial system integrity, and staying compliant with banking regulations. It also emphasizes customer experience and operational efficiency because false positives and delayed security checks can create discontent and unnecessary delays.
business_stakes_quotes: Security measures must be tight at banks, but it cannot result in customer experiences that are unnecessarily delayed, in onboarding unnecessarily, in executing transactions unnecessarily.
